#3315. How to Set Up Alexa Wishlist Alerts for Black Friday and Cyber Monday

In addition to Lifehacker, her work has been featured on Wirecutter, Tom’s Guide, and ZDNET. Emily has also worked as a travel guide around the U.S. and as a content editor. She has a masters in social work and is a licensed therapist in Utah.

Amazon’s Black Friday and Cyber Monday sale has officially started—but keeping track of the best discounts yet to land and figuring out which deals are worthwhile can be a challenge. As an alternative, you can have Alexa give you a heads-up about deals on products you already know you want to purchase, so you don’t have to spend time sorting through the noise.

Then head to the Alexa mobile app and go to More in the top left (the three horizontal lines) > Settings > Notifications > Amazon Shopping and toggle on Deal Recommendations under the Shopping Recommendations options. This ensures you’ll receive notifications for items that appear in your shopping activity.

If Alexa finds an upcoming deal on something in your Saved for Later, your Wish List, or in your Shopping Cart, you’ll receive a pop-up alert on your Echo Show display or see a yellow light ring on your Echo speaker. You can also ask, “Alexa, what are my notifications?” to hear a list of deals it has compiled thus far. You can also say "Alexa, let me know when [product name] goes on sale."

Alexa can detect deals up to 24 hours in advance, so you can either ask it to remind you again when a deal starts or request that it buy the item when the deal goes live. Simply say, “Alexa, buy it for me,” and it’ll charge the default payment and send the item to the default delivery address on your account.

#3314. ‘Friends’ Gave Its Winning Formula an Unexpected Change in Just 22 Minutes

As one of the most beloved sitcoms of all time, Friends was known for depicting a specific group of friends in New York City as they navigated their 20s and 30s. Though it was merely a fantasy to live a life like Monica, Rachel, Joey, Chandler, Ross, and Phoebe, we aspired to have friends like them. Their friendship was something of a chosen family, as they would tend to celebrate Thanksgiving as a bunch; thus, the series was known for its Thanksgiving episodes.

Often, some of the most beloved episodes of the series are remembered for their antics, hijinks, and celebrity cameos; there’s one that is often underappreciated: Season 7’s “The One Where Chandler Doesn’t Like Dogs.” In this episode, the gang's all together for another annual feast. There is a baseline festive tone, but the episode also reflects a transition. This simple holiday episode captures a softer side of the series, reflecting its evolving tone. As the characters aged and reached pivotal points in their lives, the series increasingly balanced hilarious incidents with subtle life moments. The ensemble sitcom found a rhythm with a slower pace and softer beat, shifting the blueprint into a comforting blanket.

It's time to journey back to 2000 for Season 7's eighth episode. The plot of the episode sees Rachel (Jennifer Aniston) overjoyed that her cute, adorable assistant Tag (Eddie Cahill) has joined the gang for Thanksgiving dinner, but things don’t go according to plan, causing their chance at a relationship to hit a snag. Ross (David Schwimmer) becomes obsessed with naming all 50 states before dinner, but initially falls four short. Meanwhile, Phoebe (Lisa Kudrow) is discovered hiding a cute dog named Clunkers in the apartment. The discovery forces Chandler (Matthew Perry) to admit his fear of dogs. If you removed the opening line about Thanksgiving, it could have been just any other day.

For the Thanksgiving episode, there wasn't a lot of fanfare around the holiday. The decorations were sparse. The attire was casual. And the meal, though prepared exceptionally well by Monica (Courteney Cox), was a chance for everyone to eat as one. It was a chosen family gathering. Compared to many other episodes that came before, "The One Where Chandler Doesn't Like Dogs" had a much slower pace. In fact, it was like sitting on the couch after a massive Thanksgiving feast when you're stuffed: it was relaxed. Though it might be a bit jarring to imagine, pretend the studio laughter is whisked away, and the scenes are presented as if they were the modern friend-hangout hit, Adults. There is a universe in which these slice-of-life moments could be presented in that manner, something impossible in many of the other scenarios Friends presented prior.

Friends was a show about 20-somethings living their best lives in NYC. When their 30s crept in, our friends became vulnerable as they embarked on internal reflection. Tag showing up is a big shock for Rachel, but his arrival is due to the fact that he broke up with his girlfriend. So, when he's not in the room, she asks Monica and Phoebe when it's an appropriate amount of time to make a move. Phoebe says a month, Monica says three to four, but Joey, listening in from the background, chimes in with a half hour. The punch line is present, as well as the arrival of Joey's (Matt LeBlanc) iconic "moo point" line, but this is a genuine question that marks a shift in Rachel.

She has had a thing for her hot assistant, but couldn't pursue it. Now, presented with the opportunity, their conversation reveals shared uncertainty about finding love. His worries about the future resonate with her own. She wants what Monica and Chandler have. Of course, Joey nearly ruins it all, forcing Rachel to confront her feelings. In the end, her admission becomes the pair’s beginning, as Tag seals the night with a kiss.

So no one told you life was gonna be this way.

Chandler, the king of snark, admits he hates dogs, which becomes a shocking confession for everyone. Scared by the inability to know what they are thinking, Chandler's revelation serves as a comedic element in the episode. Even when he tries to joke that either the dog goes or he goes, his reaction is met with silence as they all want the cute dog to stick around. But peel back a layer, and his shocked reaction is authentic. It gives the audience a moment to see his wall crack. He begins to show his vulnerability, once masked by wit. It's a sign of growing up. In the most Joey and Chandler fashion, they have a heart-to-heart in which Chandler has to set aside his fear to make Monica happy. His willingness to bring Clunkers back shows that Chandler can put her feelings before his discomfort.

Through all the real-life vulnerabilities of Chandler and Rachel, Ross is secluded in his own world. He becomes obsessed with chasing a goal. His fixation on naming the 50 states exposes a side of him that has strayed from years of Ross and Rachel, allowing her to move on (for now). Perhaps his biggest moment of letting go of the old Ross was when he accepted help from Joey, who previously believed there were 56 states. For someone who always attempts to be the most intellectual person in the room, he gives himself momentary grace that he's not perfect. For some of us, it takes menial tasks like this to realize we're not made of steel. As Rachel wins the boy and Chandler faces his fear, Ross finally, in the closing scene, wakes up Chandler believing he has won the game, naming the fiftieth state, Delaware, only to be reminded he has Nevada twice.

The later seasons become a show about 30-somethings growing into the individuals they’d become. The comedy was still present, but the focus was on the comfort of accepting the next stage of life. There was more focus on what it means to settle down than on "live your best life." You could see this shift especially in how some of the Thanksgiving episodes were presented. Even when Brad Pitt dropped by to reminisce about the past, the episode had a more mature aura as it recognized that the past was growing more distant.

As someone revisiting the series years later, I see Friends differently now. I understand why the Thanksgiving episodes shifted. Friends was always going to need to grow up. Our gang of six was always going to take the next steps in life, so the series did the same. As they found those moments, the show softened and became warm and comforting. The laughs and gags are still there, but it is also shaped by the reality of life.

Friends is available to stream on HBO Max in the U.S.

Ross Geller, Rachel Green, Monica Geller, Joey Tribbiani, Chandler Bing, and Phoebe Buffay are six twenty-somethings living in New York City. Over 10 years and seasons, these friends go through life lessons, family, love, drama, friendship, and comedy.

#3313. macOS 27.3 public beta 2 now available, here’s everything new

After releasing developer beta 2 of macOS 27.3 earlier this week, the company is now rolling out the public beta for users looking to try the new features ahead of next month’s official release. Here’s what’s coming.

Those came alongside several new features and tools on macOS 27.3 beta 1, including vertical tabs and adaptive dark mode in Safari, native Live Activities support, Markdown rendering in Quick Look, additional checks for potentially harmful content shared through iCloud links, and Siri AI support for Traditional Chinese, Norwegian, Turkish, and Vietnamese.

And speaking of Siri AI, macOS 27.3 also expands the assistant’s capabilities across Apple’s own apps, allowing users to perform more complex actions in Messages, Music, Calendar, Photos, and Reminders, as well as manage files and folders. Apple is also introducing new tools for third-party developers to build more advanced Siri AI integrations using Markdown-based instructions.

While macOS 27.2 was a rather uneventful update, macOS 27.3 is shaping up to be the biggest update since the release of macOS 27, and users on the public beta can now try out these new features ahead of their official release.

The release build for macOS 27.3 public beta 2 is 26C5047e, which matches the developer build.

If you’d like to join Apple’s free public beta program, visit beta.apple.com.

#3308. Nick Carter Loses Bid to Dismiss Sexual Battery Claim From Melissa Schuman

A Los Angeles County judge has rejected Backstreet Boys singer Nick Carter’s bid to dismiss a sexual battery claim brought by singer and actress Melissa Schuman.

In a new ruling obtained by Rolling Stone, the judge said the claim could proceed under a California law that took effect Jan. 1, opening a two-year revival window for otherwise time-barred claims of adult sexual abuse against individual perpetrators. Unlike the law in effect when Schuman first sued Carter, the new statute allows lawsuits against individuals without requiring plaintiffs to establish a cover-up or name a business as a defendant.

“The individual claim against defendant Carter for sexual battery is proper irrespective of the existence of a cover-up. Defendants cannot prevail on summary adjudication merely by attacking the cover-up allegations,” Los Angeles County Superior Court Judge Lisa K. Sepe-Wiesenfeld wrote in her ruling issued Monday. “There is a conflict in the evidence presented as to whether a sexual assault of plaintiff occurred. Accordingly, a triable issue of material fact is present as to the first cause of action [for sexual battery].”

Attempts to reach Carter’s lawyers were not immediately successful on Tuesday. Schuman’s attorneys, Guinness Costello and Jamie Majerus, praised the judge’s decision.

“[The] ruling moves Ms. Schuman one step closer to justice. Mr. Carter asked the court to throw out her case against him without a trial, and the court declined,” the lawyers said. “Ms. Schuman first came forward in 2017 and has waited nearly a decade to put her case in front of a jury. In May, she will finally have her day in court and the opportunity to seek the justice she deserves.”

Carter had sought to dismiss Schuman’s sexual battery claim by challenging the purported cover-up alleged in her lawsuit. He argued in filings that her “entire complaint would be time-barred except for her cover-up claim” and that there was “no viable sexual battery claim against Carter individually” without the claim of an “underlying cover-up.” Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century

In a declaration, Carter said, “At no point in time have I ever offered, solicited and/or secured a non-disclosure agreement, a confidentiality agreement, a payoff, a settlement and/or otherwise participated in silencing an alleged victim of sexual assault.”

At a Nov. 6 hearing, Carter’s lawyer, Dale Hayes Jr., argued that Schuman’s “only evidence” of a cover-up came from Shannon Ruth, who alleges Carter sexually assaulted her on tour bus outside the Tacoma Dome in Washington after a show on February 25, 2001. Ruth claims Carter told her the incident was their “special secret” and that she would go to jail if she reported it to police. Hayes argued to the judge that Ruth’s testimony was “heavily contradicted” by 13 other witnesses who testified that Carter had no opportunity to encounter Ruth the night of the alleged assault. Carter maintains he never met Ruth.

After taking two weeks to consider the arguments, Judge Sepe-Wiesenfeld ruled in Schuman’s favor, allowing the sexual battery claim to proceed. A trial is set for May 10, 2027.

Schuman first sued Carter in April 2023, alleging he raped her at his Santa Monica apartment in 2003, when she was 18, and he was 23. The former member of the pop group Dream alleges Carter gave her a sedative-laced cocktail and performed oral sex on her over her protests before raping her. The two had been cast as co-stars in the 2004 made-for-TV horror film The Hollow.

Carter, 46, previously tried to dismiss the lawsuit, arguing that the dispute belonged in Nevada, where he was already suing Schuman and two other women who accused him of rape, alleging they conspired to defame and extort him. The judge rejected the request. In July 2024, he filed a $2.5 million cross-complaint against Schuman in California, maintaining that the two had consensual sex. That’s the idea behind LiberNovo’s ergonomic chairs, which combine support that moves with you and a choice of sizes, including the Maxis range for bigger and taller users. For Black Friday, LiberNovo is taking up to 42% off in the U.S., with chairs starting at $609 and offers running November 19–30.

Adjusting a chair for your desk is one thing. Keeping that support as you change position is another. LiberNovo’s Dynamic Support System links the neck support, backrest, armrests, and seat so they move together as you recline.

The Bionic FlexFit Backrest adds eight flexible panels that contour independently. Rather than relying on a single rigid backrest, the design lets different sections follow your back as you shift or turn. Once you’ve adjusted the chair to fit, the system is designed to maintain contact through those movements with fewer manual readjustments.

Both the Omni and Maxis families offer five recline positions: 105, 115, 125, 135, and 160 degrees. That gives you options for desk work, a more relaxed position for watching a video, and a deeper recline for a break.

The Maxis Electric includes motorized lumbar adjustment and OmniStretch, a five-minute powered stretch sequence used in deep recline.

#3305. The Best Amazon Prime Benefits You Probably Don't Know About

If you’re going to commit to an Amazon Prime membership, you might as well squeeze as much as you can out of the deal. And there's a good amount of juice to squeeze there. The price you pay for Amazon depends on many factors, but regardless of how much you're paying, it's worth it for most people (we've done the math).

If you're on the fence about signing up, consider that Amazon's Black Friday and Cyber Monday sale is underway, and the company is hosting some amazing tech deals. It's a great time to sell your soul—or take advantage of the 30-day free trial—and there's a lot more to your membership than just deals and free shipping.

The standard Prime membership costs $14.99 per month or $139 per year, but there are other tiers that some people might qualify for. For example, the Amazon Prime for Young Adults program allows young adults between the ages of 18 and 24 to get all of the Prime perks for half the cost—$7.49 per month or $69 annually.

I'll be the first to admit I didn't know all of the benefits that Amazon Prime offers to its members. There are a lot more perks than people think. Here are the most impressive ones (and check out the full list):

Fast free shipping on millions of items: Depending on where you live, shipping can take one or two days, and some even come on the same day for orders of $25 or more in most areas—and it’s always free (if being shipped by the Amazon store).

Select pre-ordered items can be delivered on their release date for free (for most areas).

The option to have items delivered inside your garage with a smart garage device (depending on where you live) for $1.99 per order, or for free if you combine it with Amazon Day delivery.

Earn rewards for future purchases when you select free no-rush shipping.

The option to have all your weekly orders delivered on a specific day, to reduce waste from boxes.

Amazon Prime Visa card: Cardholders get 5% back on Amazon, Whole Foods, Chase Travel, and other purchases. Prime members who use this card extensively can earn rewards that offset the cost of membership.

A Grubhub+ and Uber Eats membership, normally $9.99 per month, which gets you free delivery on eligible orders, lower service fees, exclusive deals, and other perks as long as you remain a Prime Member (it used to be only for a year). The Uber Eats membership gets you free delivery on eligible restaurants of $25 or more.

Sharing with family or friends: Amazon Family is the existing program for sharing Prime benefits, and it allows you to add separate profiles for one other adult who lives in the same household as the primary account holder, up to four teens, and up to four child accounts. This grants access to all the standard benefits, such as free delivery, Prime Video with ads, Prime Reading, third-party benefits like Grubhub, and access to audiobooks, e-books, certain games, and Amazon Music.

Amazon Health: Prime users get One Medical access for an additional $9 per month or $99 per year. Through your devices, you’ll have 24/7 access to on-demand virtual care, plus real-life access to primary care offices in a number of U.S. cities. It accepts most major health insurance plans, too.

Amazon Pharmacy: Access to free two-day delivery and other savings on medications.

Prime Video: Prime includes unlimited streaming of movies, TV shows, and Amazon Originals with ads, which normally costs $9 per month.

Amazon Music Prime: Access to Amazon's Spotify-esque music streaming service (not to be confused with Amazon's other music streaming subscriptions).

Amazon Luna: A cloud gaming platform that offers new free games every month, free downloadable PC games, content, a monthly Twitch channel subscription, and a free channel subscription on Twitch each month for Prime Members.

Amazon Photos: Unlimited photo storage plus 5 GBs for videos and other files (which extends to members of your Family Vault).

Prime Reading: Free access to a rotating selection of e-books and magazines for Kindle or Fire tablets and Kindle apps.

Amazon's First Reads: You get up to two free e-books every month from a curated list of books handpicked by editors.

#3302. WhatsApp is raising group chat limit to 1,500 participants

WhatsApp is gradually rolling out an increase to its group chat limit, allowing up to 1,500 participants to join in, instead of the previous 1,024 cap. Here are the details.

While there are exceptions, there are generally two kinds of WhatsApp users: those who hate group chats, and those who can’t seem to be in enough of them.

If you’re in the second category, you’re likely aware that WhatsApp has steadily increased the number of participants allowed in group chats over the years, jumping from 100 to 256 in 2016, then to 512 and, soon after, to 1,024 in 2022.

Now, as spotted by WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is once again expanding that limit, raising the maximum number of participants in a group chat to 1,500.

According to the website, the new limit is rolling out to users on iOS and Android, though the rollout is gradual, meaning “not every account will see the higher limit immediately.”

WhatsApp is automatically updating existing groups to support the new limit. This means that admins do not need to take any action to unlock the higher capacity. As soon as the update becomes available to their accounts, their groups will support up to 1500 members. As a result, the update lets admins add up to 476 new members to their existing groups.

This rollout comes as WhatsApp has been working to make group chats easier to manage. Just last month, the company announced four new features, including the ability to pin messages indefinitely, share status updates within groups, filter conversations by mentions and replies, and share recent message history with new members after they join.

To read WABetaInfo’s full report, follow this link.

#3301. These 14 New Features Are Coming to iOS 27.3

Apple has been beta testing iOS 27.3 since Nov. 3. While this update isn't as large as iOS 27 proper, it's surprisingly feature-filled for a 0.3 update. This is only a beta, so anything could (and likely will) change before Apple officially launches the update. But, as it stands, iOS 27.3 tests 10 new features—including one feature the company trialed in the previous beta.

Technically, anyone with a compatible iPhone can try out iOS 27.3 right now—assuming you enroll your Apple Account in the developer program. But a word of warning: Betas can be temperamental, and could be risky. As such, I'd recommend avoiding the beta until Apple releases the public beta, which comes after a bit more testing to iron out larger issues. Either way, make sure to make a full backup of your iPhone to a Mac or PC first, as issues with the beta could result in permanent data loss.

The iPhone Duo is Apple's first foldable smartphone, but also the company's first phone since the iPhone SE 3 to ship with Touch ID. While it works well enough for unlocking your iPhone, it's still an adjustment for those of us used to Face ID. With iOS 27.3, Apple is now testing face unlock for the Duo—not Face ID, mind you. The Duo's front camera doesn't have the tech required to power Face ID or its secure protocols. Instead, this feature simply unlocks your iPhone Duo with a face scan. In addition, your Duo will still require Touch ID for Apple Pay and passwords, or after 45 minutes of inactivity. You can read more about this new feature here.

iOS 27.3 also comes with a new setting that lets you lock your iPhone Duo by closing it—as you would expect from, say, a laptop—or, dare I say, a flip phone? Currently, closing the Duo seamlessly transitions what's on the big screen to the smaller display, and you have to press the side button to lock the phone.

With watchOS 27, Apple released "Audio Intelligence," a new set of features for Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. Audio Intelligence uses the watches' new S11 chip, along with on-device AI and cloud-based AI, to run new features, like Sound Recognition and Shazam (music recognition).

With iOS 27.3, however, the company is now officially testing the other two Audio Intelligence features it originally announced with watchOS 27. First, there's Live Rewind: By double-clicking the watch crown, you can pull up a transcript of the last 15 seconds of a conversation. Siri Recap, on the other hand, displays summaries of conversations you had that day, in case you need a refresher on any chats you might have otherwise forgotten about,

The company generated some controversy when it first announced these two Audio Intelligence features, since, on the surface, it sounds like these new Apple Watches are essentially spying on people all day long. According to Apple, however, that isn't really the case. The company says Audio Intelligence is private, and never records or stores any audio. No speakers are ever identified, and text results (both transcripts and summaries) are deleted automatically after a set period of time unless the user saves them to the Siri app. You can read more about how Audio Intelligence works here.

Despite their claims, I'm sure there will still be strong feelings surrounding these Audio Intelligence features. We'll have to see whether Apple can prove Live Rewind and Siri Recap aren't all that creepy throughout the iOS 27.3 beta process.

iOS 27.3 also introduces app actions for Siri AI. Apple is testing new abilities for Siri AI, including organizing files, planning events, or adding photos to albums. You could ask Siri to organize your Downloads folder, or delete files that haven't been opened in more than a year. You could ask Siri to find a coffee shop you went to last week, or to save an article to your Reading List in Safari. You could ask Siri to check your calendar and set up a time for an event based on when you're free. You can even ask the assistant to schedule, edit, or unsend messages.

For example, you could ask Siri AI to help you plan a trip with your friends. You could ask the AI to put together a themed playlist in Apple Music, schedule a message to a group about an upcoming trip, organize the websites you've been visiting in Safari into a tab group, and, after the trip, ask Siri to move your best photos to your favorites album. These new actions work in the following apps: Calendar, Files, Finder, Journal, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Notes, Photos, Preview, Reminders, Safari, Shortcuts, and Weather. Developers can also add Siri AI app actions support to their own apps.

Apple started testing its new Health app with the iOS 27.2 beta, but pulled the redesign before the official release. Now, with iOS 27.3, the new app is back. The new Health app has a health dashboard for the first time, as well as new features like Health Age and movement assessments. It seems to be pulling from some popular competitor services, hopefully, for the better. For more on the new Health app, check out Lifehacker health editor Beth Skwarecki's explainer.

Continuing on the Health track, iOS 27.3 also introduces "Gym Strength." This is a new Fitness+ feature that offers a personalized four-week strength-training plan. You can customize these plans to meet your goals, experience level, and schedule, and they adapt as you progress. You'll get recommendations based on your experience with exercises, reps, and sets, including video demos for exercises. You can access Gym Strength on both iPhone and iPad, and Apple Watches are optional—though you can log your progress with the wearable if you have it.

Apple is also testing a new Siri AI feature in Safari, that gives the bot access to entire webpages, including the parts of the site that aren't on-screen. Say you want to know all the gluten-free options on a menu on a restaurant's website, but only a portion of the site is actually in view. You could ask Siri to read you the gluten-free options, and it would pull from the whole page, even though you can only see part of it.

Vertical tabs have been a favorite among browser aficionados, as they give you more screen real estate in your browser while keeping your tabs off the side. Apple hasn't made the jump—until now. This feature works with iPads running iPadOS 27.3 as well as Macs running macOS 27.3.

Another new Safari feature in testing is "Adaptive Dark Mode." This feature forces websites into a dark theme, if they don't have a native theme of their own. There are third-party apps that can do this, but this is the first time Apple has offered this feature built into Safari.

Apple is also testing new StandBy experiences with iOS 27.3, which were previously only available on the iPhone Duo. When you turn your iPhone sideways while plugged in, you'll find new Analog and Digital Clock faces with new customization options. There's also a new Photos face, with the option to pull images from Shared Albums.

"Reachability" pulls your iPhone's display down towards the bottom of the screen, so you can access items towards the top of the display with one hand. It's a useful feature for those of us with big iPhones, and now, there's no iPhone bigger than the Duo. With iOS 27.3, Apple is testing Reachability for its first foldable phone. It's a bit like the inverse of how Reachability currently works: You can swipe on the left or right side of your Duo's display to shift the other side of the screen towards your current position. If you're holding your Duo in your left hand, a swipe of the left side will pull the right side over to the left, and vice versa.

Apple is also rolling out new languages for Siri AI in iOS 27.3. Now, Apple's smart assistant supports Traditional Chinese, Vietnamese, Turkish, and Norwegian.

If you have an Apple Intelligence-compatible iPad running iPadOS 27.3, you now have access to Siri Mode in Camera. As with iOS, you can open the Camera app on iPadOS to access Siri Mode, and ask Siri about your surroundings.

If you watch videos in Apple Podcasts, you can find them in more sources than the Podcasts app. With the new updates, you'll find these videos on Apple TV 4K, select smart TVs, your iPhone, iPad, Mac, and even in CarPlay. (Please don't watch video podcasts while driving.)

#3299. CIA Cyberattack Adds to Growing List of Major Security Breaches, Report

The Central Intelligence Agency is the latest government agency to fall victim to a cyberattack ... adding to a growing list of digital security scares that have rocked the country in recent weeks.

An unclassified CIA system was breached by hackers, according to the Associated Press, which cites a person familiar with the situation.

The good news ... no classified information was compromised, and the breach has reportedly been resolved. The bad news? Nobody seems to know who's behind it.

The targeted system handles what's known as open-source intelligence ... essentially information collected from publicly available sources, including websites and commercial databases.

As TMZ previously reported ... the FBI was recently targeted in a suspected cyberattack involving its national criminal information database. That's on top of another massive cyberattack targeting 178 websites, including major companies and online platforms.

And let's not forget the nationwide FAA ground stop that brought air travel to a standstill earlier this month ... though there's no evidence linking that disruption to the CIA breach or the other cyber incidents.

The latest breach raises even more questions about the security of America's digital infrastructure ... especially with so many systems coming under scrutiny in such a short period.

#3296. Karen Read’s Murder Trial Made Her Famous. A New Doc Explores the Story People Don’t Know

It’s been almost five years since Canton, Massachusetts resident Karen Read found the body of her police-officer boyfriend John O’Keefe unresponsive in the snow in the early hours of Jan. 29, 2022. Since that day, the circumstances around O’Keefe’s death and the subsequent investigation have turned Read into one of the most divisive murder defendants in the nation. Now, a new docuseries is tackling the internet-famous case and the behind-the-scenes details people don’t know.

Directed by Danielle Johnson Cutts and released Nov. 23, The Trials of Karen Read charts Read’s journey from unknown Canton resident to a true-crime mainstay. The fervor around Read’s trial was complicated by social media accounts alleging a police conspiracy was using Read as a scapegoat. The series’ biggest revelations focus less on chasing down the minute details of Read’s defense and more on building out a picture of O’Keefe that his family and friends say was lost in the fervor of Read’s case.

“The intention was always to make a well-rounded series, and we wanted to try and tell this story from multiple firsthand perspectives,” Johnson Cutts told Netflix’s Tudum. She added that O’Keefe’s friends and family only spoke to “center John [in the story] and remind what has now become a global audience of their pain: [the fact] that they have lost a father figure, a brother, and a son. And that has very, very much been lost in the melee of the trials of Karen Read.”

It was supposed to be a routine night. On Jan. 28, 2022, Read and O’Keefe met friends at Canton’s Waterfall Bar and Grille and the group decided to keep the hangout going at the home of Brian Albert, a fellow police officer. Read has maintained that she was driving under the influence and has a shoddy memory of the night. She told police she dropped O’Keefe off at the house and returned in the early hours when she realized he hadn’t made it home, where she found him unresponsive in a snowbank. Police have a different theory: They believe Read backed up into O’Keefe with her car and then left him to freeze to death. She was arrested and charged with second-degree murder, manslaughter while operating under the influence of alcohol, and leaving the scene of personal injury and death. Read’s first trial, which started on April 16, 2024, ended with a mistrial. And at her second trial, which began on April 1, 2025, a jury acquitted Read of all charges except drunk driving, leaving her a free woman.  Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century

“Johnny was the strong one and the pillar of strength,” O’Keefe’s brother, Paul O’Keefe, says in the documentary. “You want someone to be held accountable for taking a loved one from you. We just want justice for our loss.”

Read and her representatives declined to participate in the three-part docuseries, but it does include  interviews from O’Keefe’s friends, family, and investigators involved in the case. It also shows some never-before-seen footage, including police cameras, O’Keefe’s home videos, and unreleased audio from an interview Read did in 2023 with Boston Magazine.

“At the end of the day this was about John O’Keefe. And his death has become an absolute circus,” Jen McCabe, Albert’s sister-in-law, says in the docuseries. “People have profited off it and people have used it to destroy so many lives and the victim and his family, they lost. People should remember John and the amazing guy he was. Not Karen Read.”

Here are four things we learned from The Trials of Karen Read.

Read and O’Keefe dated briefly in 2004 but reconnected after the Covid-19 pandemic. When they started dating exclusively in 2020, Canton residents and close friends of O’Keefe say that the two seemed very happy with each other. O’Keefe was the legal guardian of his niece and nephew, Kayley and Patrick Furbush, and they quickly welcomed Read into the fold. In her interview with Boston Magazine, Read said she didn’t want to replace their deceased parents but wanted to be as helpful as possible — often staying over for days on end or making sure she was at recitals and sporting events with O’Keefe.  Related Content ‘Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth’ Isn't a Sequel. It’s a ‘GTA: Tarantino’ Side Mission ‘A Lot of Fighting’: What Happened Before Courtney Clenney Killed Christian Obumseli? Why Did Three Men Spend 36 Years in Prison for a Murder They Didn’t Commit? Matthew McConaughey Is Hype for U2’s Thanksgiving Eve NFL Halftime Show

“She treated me like a friend,” Kayley, now about 18, says in the documentary. “She’s funny. She was always laughing or making us laugh. She meshed really well with me and my brother. I definitely thought Karen was going to be someone I could talk to and relate with the way my friends got to with their moms. That was exciting.”

In the docuseries, O’Keefe’s friends say Read quickly fit into the group. “She was super nice. She was friendly. She was funny. She was outgoing,” McCabe says. “I loved her. I think John loved having a companion and someone to go out and have a good time with.”

McCabe, who was friends with both O’Keefe and Read, was with Read when she discovered O’Keefe’s body, and says the scene was immediately chaotic. But even after police left, O’Keefe’s family and friends had unanswered questions about how exactly he died. When police arrested Read on Feb. 1, their theory was that Read had accidentally hit O’Keefe with her car and was so drunk she didn’t notice. But further investigations, including a data pull from her car, revealed her back up cameras and sensors were completely functional, making an accidental strike unlikely.

Read’s case quickly caught the attention of online true-crime enthusiasts. One of the most prominent YouTubers who first posted about the case was Aidan Kearney, known as Turtleboy on YouTube. Kearney posted dozens of videos claiming Read was being set up by the Canton Police Department; popularizing alternative theories about O’Keefe’s death, including the possibility of a fight inside Albert’s home or a dog attack. (Kearney did not participate in the documentary). He often showed up to homes of O’Keefe’s friends, or confronted them in public places like sporting events. He also hosted several “Free Karen Read” rallies and protests, one of which involved marching protestors by the homes of Albert and McCabe. He was especially focused on Colin Albert, a teen who he believed might have fought with O’Keefe and accidentally killed him.

In the docuseries, Albert speaks out in a rare public interview and says Kearney’s video sent waves of targeted harassment towards him, both online and in person. “I am not the kid that these people were making me out as,” he says. “I am scared every single day about somebody coming up to me, whether they try to attack me, whether they try to do something horrible. I’m scared every day of my life for that.”

During Read’s first trial, her defense team uncovered multiple text messages from

Massachusetts State Police Trooper Michael Proctor, the lead investigator on her case, in which he referred to Read as a “bitch,” and a “wack job cunt,” adding “hopefully she kills herself.” This eroded trust in his investigation, and Proctor was fired in 2025 after months of suspension. On Nov. 10, Massachusetts State Police and Read settled a civil lawsuit alleging police misconduct during her arrest and trial.  The suit claimed the department had “an embedded culture of bigotry, misogyny, systemic failures” and cited Proctor’s text messages.

“I feel like I let down the O’Keefe family. I feel like I let down my family. I let down the state police, the DA’s office,” Proctor says in the docuseries, a rare look into his feelings on the public misstep. “I just feel like I let down so many people.”

Two jurors for Read’s second trial, identified only by their first names in the docuseries, say that Read’s case was so big that the jurors couldn’t avoid news about it before the trial. Many of the people on the jury were aware of Read’s case before they heard any testimony and several were familiar with the internet theories of a police coverup or conspiracy.

“I don’t know if it was possible to find a jury that was a completely blank slate,” Jason, a juror, says in the series.  Trending Stories Billy Ray Cyrus Shares Snapshots From Miley’s Wedding: ‘Beautiful’ to See Family ‘United by Love’ U2 Will Bring Their ‘Greatest Show on Earth’ Stadium Tour to North America in 2027 Chris Christie to Republicans: ‘I Don’t Want to Hear Your Whining’ Anthem Singer Apologizes for ‘O Canada’ Flub at Leafs-Islanders Game

While the jury was torn on whether actual police corruption occurred, both jurors say that there were too many holes in the evidence and available testimony to prove that Read was guilty beyond a reasonable doubt. It’s a defining characteristic that not only determined Read’s fate but has continued to dog her case.

“I really did think, most likely, that she did it,” Janet, the other juror, says. “But I think by our legal system’s standards, she’s not guilty because there were so many different possibilities. He could’ve gone into the house, he could’ve gotten beaten up, he could’ve got hit by a plow. It’s almost like ‘doubt, doubt, doubt’ kinda hanging out there. It was a lot of doubt — it was more than reasonable doubt.”

#3291. ‘You Can See Everything’ Gets Digital Release — Here’s Where You Can Stream It

If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Rolling Stone may receive an affiliate commission.

You Can See Everything was one of the biggest breakout movies of the year, racking up positive reviews, big box office numbers, and awards buzz — a rarity for a nearly three-hour documentary.

Despite the fact that it’s still showing in theaters, You Can See Everything is available to stream at home; the film is available to rent for $19.99 or buy for $24.99 on PVOD platforms like Amazon, Apple TV, and Fandango at Home.

Distributor A24 has not yet announced a Blu-ray or subscription streaming release. The film will eventually land on HBO Max because of A24’s pay-1 deal with the streaming service.

You Can See Everything, directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, ups the ante on Fielder’s brand of intimate, awkward interactions. In the film, he spends over a month living with Elizabeth Holmes and her partner, Billy Evans, just before Holmes heads to prison for financial crimes related to her failed biotech company, Theranos. The documentary also marks a major year for Oppenheim, who helmed this year’s acclaimed Robert Pattinson-starring Primetime.

You Can See Everything features a surprisingly significant appearance by Amanda Seyfried, who played Holmes in the Hulu series The Dropout. The series was one of a number of films and books about Holmes, whose case became one of the most notorious financial crimes of the 21st century. Yet somehow, You Can See Everything managed to frame the story in an entirely new light, in part thanks to Seyfried’s appearance.

In an extensive interview with Rolling Stone, Seyfried discussed her eagerness to be a part of the film with Fielder and Oppenheim. “When you needed me, I came because of how invested you were, and how I felt like we were all on the same page at a point,” she said to the co-directors. “We were like a band. We were like a team. It felt like part of the team. And when I felt part of the team, it made me want to go even further. It’s not necessarily about being safe, but about doing something different.”

#3289. iOS 27.3: New features, release date, more

iOS 27.3 is currently in beta testing with developers and public beta users. The update includes multiple new features for iPhone users, including the redesigned Health app, iPhone Duo updates, and much more. Here’s everything you need to know about what’s new in iOS 27.3 …

9to5Mac is supported by Sony: Score Sony’s ULT Field 1 Bluetooth speaker for 51% off. Powerful bass, room-filling sound, up to 12 hours of battery life, IP67 durability, stereo pairing support, and much more.

As my colleague Ryan explained, Apple will likely release iOS 27.3 to all iPhone users sometime in December. Typically, Apple would release its x.2 software updates in December, but this year is different because iOS 27.1 was exclusive to iPhone Duo. That means that, in terms of the timeline, iOS 27.3 is essentially the equivalent of iOS 27.2.

Here’s when Apple has released its December updates in recent years:

So with that in mind, we expect iOS 27.3 to be released sometime during the first half of December.

The redesigned Health app is back in iOS 27.3. This was first available during testing of iOS 27.2, but did not ship as part of that final update.

The redesigned Health app is split into three tabs: Insights, Longevity, and Browse. The app features an all-new design that dynamically adapts based on your data, including Apple Intelligence. The Longevity tab includes a new Health age feature that uses Apple Watch data to show how your metrics track relative to your actual age.

For Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 users, it also offers easy access to view your Readiness score every morning.

For Apple Fitness+, iOS 27.3 adds a new Gym Strength feature. This creates progressive, four-week plans based on your strength goals, experience, schedule, and available equipment.

As you complete each week of workouts, the following week adapts based on the reps and weights you logged.

For iPhone Duo users, iOS 27.3 adds Reachability support. This setting shifts the interface on the outer display to the right or left, making it easier to reach the far corners. It’s designed to make iPhone Duo easier to use with one hand, despite the wider outer display. You activate it by swiping right on the right edge of the screen or left on the left edge.

Reachability for iPhone Duo is on by default. You can turn it off in Settings > Accessibility > Touch > Reachability.

iOS 27.3 also brings a new face unlock feature to iPhone Duo. This is not full-fledged Face ID. Instead, Apple is using the front-facing camera on the iPhone Duo’s outer display to recognize you, then unlock the device. It doesn’t work for things like Apple Pay and passwords.

iOS 27.3 also tweaks the iPhone Duo’s software keyboard by making the keys slightly narrower and the font slightly smaller.

Finally, iOS 27.3 includes a new option in the Settings app to have your iPhone Duo lock when closed. Once enabled, your iPhone Duo will lock when you fold it, rather than transition content from the inner display to the outer display.

When it debuted, the iPhone Duo included a more robust version of StandBy with new clock faces and expanded customization options. iOS 27.3 brings the iPhone Duo’s StandBy experience to all iPhone models.

This includes the redesigned Analog and Digital Clock faces, as well as additional customization options for colors and complications. The update also adds support for Shared Albums to the Photos face.

iOS 27.3 brings several key Siri AI updates. First, the update expands Siri AI with many new capabilities across Apple apps. Apple explains:

We started rolling out these new capabilities across many Apple apps, including Calendar, Files, Finder, Journal, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Notes, Photos, Preview, Reminders, Safari, Shortcuts, and Weather, so users can do things like find a coffee shop they visited last week or archive files that haven’t been opened in over a year.

There are many more actions available now as examples for you to reference. To see what you can do in each app, just ask Siri AI.

With iOS 27.3, Apple is also starting to test new ways for developers to create Siri AI integrations for the first time. This is described as an “early Developer Preview.” Apple explains:

Today’s preview allows any app to bring its content and actions directly into Siri AI by using App Intents, making it easier for all apps to tap into Siri AI’s newest capabilities, including personal context understanding, onscreen awareness, natural language, and more. So people can just ask for help in their own words, and Siri AI carries out any custom action you’ve built, from checking a delivery to booking a reservation to placing an order.

While this is being tested as part of iOS 27.3, Apple says it will start shipping to customers in a few months.

iOS 27.3 also expands Siri AI to new languages, including French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish.

iOS 27.3 also introduces usage limits on select Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features. The limits apply to things like:

You can unlock higher usage limits with an eligible iCloud+ plan, starting at $2.99 per month. If you hit your usage limit, basic Siri requests will still work. That includes things like setting timers and alarms.

iOS 27.3 brings the original set of Apple Intelligence features to China for the first time. This does not include Siri AI or other iOS 27 updates, but it does include the following features:

iOS 27.3 is a major update to Safari. First, the update adds support for a new vertical tabs design layout on iPhone Duo’s inner display. If you choose this option, your Safari tabs will be arranged vertically along the left-hand side of Safari, rather than along the top. Vertical tabs are also available on Mac and iPad with macOS 27.3 and iPadOS 27.3.

iOS 27.3 also adds a new Adaptive Dark Mode feature. This feature can automatically apply Dark Mode to websites that don’t natively support it. You can choose to have Adaptive Dark Mode automatically kick in or use it on a site-by-site basis.

For Apple Music users, iOS 27.3 adds a new “Selfie Sing” feature that lets users record a video of themselves while singing karaoke. To use this feature, start playing a song and go to the lyrics view. Then tap the new camera button that appears on the right-hand side of the lyrics.

The update also refines the design of viewing lyrics while your iPhone is in landscape mode.

There are two key changes to the Apple TV app in iOS 27.3. First, the update introduces video podcasts in the TV app. You can now watch your favorite video podcasts in the TV app, and sync your playback progress between the TV app and the Podcasts app.

Second, iOS 27.3 adds vertical video to the TV app. The app now includes a new “Explore Clip Collections” section where you can browse clips from Apple TV content in a TikTok-style design.

#3283. Apple’s ‘just works’ approach is great, but goes a little too far

“It just works” is one of the phrases most commonly associated with Apple. Interestingly, it appears to have been coined by the company’s customers and then used by reviewers before it was later picked up by Steve Jobs.

Of course, it’s now commonly used ironically when Apple products don’t do what they are supposed to (Apple Home, I’m looking at you), but I do think that it’s absolutely the right philosophy and goal – most of the time …

Macworld referenced an Apple brochure from 1996 entitled “Why do people prefer Macintosh?” This is a collection of testimonials from customers, a number of whom use the “it just works” phrasing. It was subsequently used by a number of reviewers. The earliest example I can find of Steve Jobs adopting it was in 1999, when discussing the rollout of FireWire to the Mac in the PowerMac G3.

It’s hot-pluggable. You don’t have to turn your computer off to connect and disconnect peripherals, you can just plug them right in. Again, the drivers are dynamically loaded. There are no terminators and there are no switches. It just works.

(If you have a link to any earlier example, please do let me know in the comments.)

I’m a big fan of the philosophy. Most of the time, users should just be able to get on with the tasks they want to execute without having to worry about the technology. The tech that makes it all possible should sit there quietly in the background.

However, there are cases where I think Apple takes this approach a little too far, and where tech-savvy users at least would like a little more transparency and control.

AirPods firmware updates are a good example. Back in September, there was quite a significant update in the form of custom EQ. It’s a rather basic version, but still a feature many had wanted for a long time. Instead of being able to manually trigger the update, users had to wait until it “just worked.”

Apple’s support document has a how-to guide that is essentially an outline of the conditions required to permit an update, and an instruction to simply wait until it happens. Which you will only know by repeatedly checking.

Make sure your AirPods are connected via Bluetooth to your iPhone, iPad or Mac. Connect your charging case to a power source. Put your AirPods in their charging case and close the lid. Keep the lid of the charging case closed, and keep your AirPods in Bluetooth range of your iPhone, iPad or Mac. Wait at least 30 minutes for the firmware to be updated. Check the firmware version again.

Another example, and one I’ve complained about before, is that there is no way to manually trigger an iCloud document sync, nor any progress indicator when it does finally happen. In the best of cases, it takes seconds; in the worst, many hours. And again, the only way to find out is to repeatedly check.

It’s the same story when shooting a video on your iPhone. Will it still be there an hour later, available to instantly edit and view? Maybe, or maybe it will have been offloaded to the cloud, requiring it to be downloaded before you can do anything with it – while a video you shot months earlier is still stored locally on the device! You can, of course, switch off optimization altogether, but if you choose to use it, you get no control over it. I want a setting that allows me to do things like specify local retention of all photos and videos taken within the past fortnight.

Will that video be available in the Mac Photos app when you check half an hour later? Maybe, maybe not. You can click the Sync Now button as many times as you like, and it will apparently have no effect, claiming it’s up to date despite the video being entirely absent. It will be there when it’s there.

Once it is in the Photos app on your Mac, it’s a similar story when exporting it to a folder. You can drag and drop the video into the folder, and this time you are manually triggering the transfer (yay!), but there will be absolutely no visual indication that it is in progress. No grayed-out icon, no progress bar, nothing. So far as the user interface is concerned, it appears that your drag and drop had no effect – until the video file finally appears.

I think with all of these things and more, Apple needs to offer options. Yes, most non-tech users may be perfectly happy to just wait until things happen, but there ought to be a standard way to trigger things that currently happen in their own sweet time, as well as progress indicators and confirmation that a process is complete.

Is this an ecosystem-wide improvement you’d like to see? Please share your thoughts in the comments and add any frustrating examples of your own.

#3279. 'Wifi Motion Sensing' Can Track Everything You Do Through Your Router

A simple wifi feature could let ISPs track your location and movement patterns within your home. "Wifi motion sensing" turns your ISP’s router into a motion detector, letting providers know exactly how many people are in the house, where they are situated, individual movement patterns, and, in some cases, even body shapes that could approximate a person’s identity.

Wifi routers rely on radio signals to connect wirelessly to your devices and appliances. Those same radio signals are also absorbed and reflected by the human body as they travel in all directions from the router. With the right software, ISPs can track how those wifi signals travel around your room, which can be studied to detect presence and sense motion patterns.

As long as your ISP’s router model supports this feature natively, it doesn’t require any additional hardware to be installed in your home. For example, Xfinity’s version of the feature pairs your router with five other connected appliances in your room to create oval-shaped sensing zones that can track your presence and movement within those spaces.

It isn’t a new feature, either—companies like Cognitive Systems and Origin Wireless that supply networking hardware to ISPs have been offering wifi motion sensing for years now, while early research prototypes from the MIT date back at least as far as 2015. In 2025, IEEE updated its Wi-Fi 802.11 standard to include motion sensing and lay out the architectural guidelines for it, which makes it likely that even more routers will now ship with the feature.

In its current consumer form, wifi motion sensing can help you control smart home apparatus like lights or thermostats, get pet safety notifications on your phone, set up a fall alert system for elderly users, and trigger appliances remotely based on human presence. But enabling it carries risks.

Most providers, including Cognitive Systems, claim that the technology isn’t sensitive to identity and can’t be used to track specific individuals. But even if true, that’s more likely to be a product decision rather than a technical limitation. Karlsruhe Institute researchers have shown that even ordinary wifi signals can identify individuals with a 99.5% accuracy.

Also worth noting: ISPs’ legal wording suggests that they may disclose the collected and stored motion data at any time to law enforcement, government agencies, regulators, and courts in response to subpoenas or during an emergency. ISPs may also retain your motion data in the cloud long-term in case they are required to facilitate a subpoena in the future.

As far as major ISPs are concerned, Xfinity (Comcast) is the only broadband provider that currently offers this feature across its commercial routers on the XB7, XB8, XB9, XB10, MXB1, and XER10 gateways. It’s opted out by default, but in case you or a family member already switched it on, you can disable it again by navigating to Home > WiFi Motion on the Xfinity app, click on the gear icon on the live view page, and tap Remove WiFi Motion.

Verizon Fios customers also had access to a Home Awareness feature on their routers that could be toggled on or off using the MyFios app, but that’s since been discontinued. In an official disclosure published shortly after the discontinuation, Verizon notified customers that it has deleted all associated movement logs from this service and no longer retains any motion data from users.

But there are other regional ISPs that offer it, too. For example, Breezeline (Atlantic Broadband) offers a feature called Motion within its Plume-powered application that alerts customers when movement is detected in their homes, among its other features. MidCo, a telecom company in the Upper Midwest, has a feature called Sense which can be toggled on or off using the MidCo Wi-Fi app. Plume, ADT-owned Origin Wireless, and Airties—all of whom supply technology to ISPs—have also been marketing motion sensing to customers for the last few years.

If you’re unsure if your wifi router or ISP has motion sensing features or opts you in by default, look for a feature called “Sense,” “Motion,” or equivalent in your broadband’s mobile app. Exact steps differ greatly from one ISP to another, so it’s best not to assume that they will all opt you out by default, or that they collect the same types of data. With the 802.11bf update to IEEE standards in 2025, this technology will be accessible to even more router manufacturers, so expect adoption to grow among internet providers as well.

#3278. Don Was Pays Tribute to Bobby Weir by Reimagining a Classic Dead Album

When Blues for Allah was recorded by the Grateful Dead at Bob Weir’s home studio in 1975, the band had been looking far to the east, incorporating North African melodies and instrumentation to accompany lyricist Robert Hunter’s conceptual imagery. Some 50 years later, noted producer and Blue Note Records president Don Was only had to travel to the midwest to interpret the songs of the seminal album (fan favorites “The Music Never Stopped,” “Help on the Way/Slipknot,” and “Franklin’s Tower” among them), linking with jazz trumpeter and composer Terence Blanchard for a one-off show for his curated Paradise Jazz Series at the Detroit Symphony Orchestra.

The idea of revisiting Blues for Allah was prompted by Laina Cohen, the Golden Road Festival founder who suggested Was and his band perform the album at the 2025 gathering in Buford, Georgia, to celebrate the LP’s golden anniversary. After years of playing with Bobby Weir and the Wolf Bros, Was was the ideal candidate to reinterpret the album with elements of blues and jazz and a Detroit swing. The only problem was he didn’t have his own band. So, Was set forth to form one.

“I called people who I knew were awesome musicians, but I also knew we all grew up listening to the same radio stations and playing in the same bars and playing for the same tough audiences,” he says. “They’re open and receptive and as enthusiastic as you can be.” Dubbed “the Pan Detroit-Ensemble,”  the group, featuring saxophonist and Blue Note Records artist Dave McMurray, keyboardist Luis Resto, trombonist Vincent Chandler, and vocalist Steffanie Christi’an, proved to be the perfect vehicle.

Still, confronting the odd time signatures and elaborate instrumentation of the album left Was stumped. “‘King Solomon’s Marbles’ was one that really required some work,” he says. “I always thought it was just a jam, and I thought the reason it didn’t get played was because it was just something that happened once. As we got into it, I realized there’s actually a very specific and clearly delineated structure to the song.”  Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century

Was worried the fan base wouldn’t respond positively. “I was [concerned] that we’d gone too far for some fans, that it was sacred ground, but it wasn’t the case at all,” he says. “No one ever had a problem with adapting it because they could tell it was done in service to the song.”

“Crazy Fingers” was another tough song for Was and his band. “We used to play that in Wolf Bros, and it’s sort of reggae, sort of Irving Berlin. It’s a very weird feeling, and if you don’t get it exactly right, it falls flat,” he says. “It didn’t come naturally to nine people from Detroit. So what did come naturally was to turn it into a six-eight thing like Otis Redding’s ‘Dreams to Remember.’”

Was started working on this project before Weir’s death last January, and played some of the music for his longtime friend and bandmate.  “He dug it. And my guess is that had he survived a year, he’d have come out and played some,” Was says. “He heard a little rehearsal thing, and he’d seen YouTube stuff of  ‘Shakedown Street’ and ‘Loser‘” in our very first shows, and he loved it. He was very proactive about making sure that the music would outlive all of us, and he really welcomed that.”

As fate would have it, the first date of Was’s Blues for Allah tour fell on the day Weir died. “We were in Ann Arbor, Michigan, and I had to go out and tell them. I didn’t feel like doing it, but I remembered Bobby talking a lot about the night Jerry died, and they were in New Hampshire, and they went out and played. He said, ‘You bring comfort to people by playing good music for them.’ So we played the songs, and then I went out and sat with the audience for a while, and we talked about Bobby, and everyone had stories to tell. I found it incredibly comforting. For all the subsequent shows, it became a place to go and grieve.”  Related Content Grateful Dead's Official Blanket, Towel, and Poncho Collab Is 20% Off for Black Friday The Restless Storytelling at the Heart of the Grateful Dead Bill Kreutzmann Plans ‘A Very Grateful Thanksgiving’ in Hawaii My Morning Jacket Connect the Grateful Dead Dots in Faithful San Francisco Residency

Was and the band toured throughout the year and on Nov. 20 released their own live version of Blues for Allah.  Trending Stories Billy Ray Cyrus Shares Snapshots From Miley’s Wedding: ‘Beautiful’ to See Family ‘United by Love’ U2 Will Bring Their ‘Greatest Show on Earth’ Stadium Tour to North America in 2027 Chris Christie to Republicans: ‘I Don’t Want to Hear Your Whining’ Anthem Singer Apologizes for ‘O Canada’ Flub at Leafs-Islanders Game

Bobby’s presence is still felt. As Was shares, “The weird thing is that I don’t feel like he’s gone. He’s ubiquitous, man. You turn on SiriusXM radio anytime, and he’s on, and the music’s everywhere, and we’re out playing the music. When he talked about Jerry, he would say that he could feel like Jerry was kind of on his shoulder. I thought he was being hyperbolic, but I liked the image of it. It’s actually how I feel. I kind of got him in there when I’m playing, because I’m used to playing these songs with him, and playing in the Wolf Bros changed the way I played in a big way.”

And like the Dead, the musical experimentation continues: Was’s next project is the Dead’s prog epic Terrapin Station, coinciding with the album’s 50th anniversary in 2027.

#3277. Apple Calendar got two feature upgrades it really needed in iOS 27

Apple Calendar keeps getting better, including some design updates coming in iOS 27.3. But there are two standout feature upgrades added recently in iOS 27 that Apple’s Calendar app really needed.

I’ve used Apple’s Calendar app for years, and there’s an elegant simplicity to it. But one key area the app has long lagged behind competitors is event creation.

When you need to create a new event, the Calendar app historically has required manually filling in various fields for the title, date, time, invitees, etc. By contrast, the excellent third-party app Fantastical lets you type in natural language and it automatically fills in relevant parameters based on what you type.

In iOS 27, Apple finally introduces its own natural language input for Calendar events. You can type out your event details and certain recognized parameters will be used to automatically fill in the detail fields.

While the feature still isn’t on par with what Fantastical offers, since it doesn’t support as many data points as the third-party alternative, it’s very much a step in the right direction.

Apple has always pitched Siri as being like a personal assistant. As such, calendar-related tasks should have been Siri’s strong suit. But until iOS 27, you couldn’t actually manage your calendar very well using Siri.

With Siri AI, that’s changed in a big way. Now, you can do things like:

One of my favorite personal examples is from this summer when the NFL schedule was released. I asked Siri to find the Dallas Cowboys schedule and add every game to my calendar, and it pulled this off with ease.

Siri is so much better than before at assisting with your calendar, and iOS 27.3 will bring even more capabilities soon.

What are your favorite iOS 27 Apple Calendar upgrades? Let us know in the comments.
